options.A: Priya cleared GATE with a top rank.

questions.question: [MCQ] The figure below shows a flat net made of six equal squares, which is folded along all edges to form a closed cube used to pack a small sensor module.Figure: Net of six squares (P, Q, R, S, T, U) to be folded into a cube When the net is folded into a cube, which face becomes exactly OPPOSITE to face P?

Q, R, S and T are attached directly to P's top, right, bottom and left edges respectively, and fold up to become the Top, Right, Bottom and Left faces — each adjacent to Front, not opposite. questions.solution:

options.C: det(A) can be any real number depending on A

options.B: Radial flow of groundwater towards the well, producing a drawdown that decreases with radial distance from the well
options.C: A decrease in hydraulic conductivity near the well

questions.solution:

options.B: Parboiling of paddy before milling generally increases the head-rice yield (proportion of unbroken milled rice) compared to milling raw (non-parboiled) paddy.
options.C: The degree of milling (polishing) of rice has no effect on its nutrient (e.g. vitamin B1/thiamine) content.
options.D: Aspiration/winnowing in grain cleaning primarily separates materials based on differences in their terminal (settling) velocity in an air stream.

questions.solution:

questions.question: [MSQ — one or more correct] Which of the following statement(s) about heat exchangers in dairy/food processing is/are CORRECT?

options.A: The logarithmic mean temperature difference (LMTD) is used to determine the effective average temperature driving force in a heat exchanger with a varying temperature profile along its length.
options.B: In counter-current (counter-flow) heat exchangers, the outlet temperature of the cold fluid can, in principle, exceed the outlet temperature of the hot fluid.
options.C: In parallel-flow (co-current) heat exchangers, the same is also true — the cold fluid's outlet temperature can exceed the hot fluid's outlet temperature.
options.D: The thermal conductivity of a food material generally increases with increasing moisture content.

questions.solution:
Q.63 Solution:• Correct Answer: A, B, D• Section: Agricultural Engineering | Sub-topic: Heat and Mass Transfer | Type: MSQ | Marks: 2Q.63  |  S7 — Dairy & Food Engineering  |  Heat and Mass TransferType: MSQ   |   Marks: 2Question:Which of the following statement(s) about heat exchangers in dairy/food processing is/are CORRECT?(A) The logarithmic mean temperature difference (LMTD) is used to determine the effective average temperature driving force in a heat exchanger with a varying temperature profile along its length.(B) In counter-current (counter-flow) heat exchangers, the outlet temperature of the cold fluid can, in principle, exceed the outlet temperature of the hot fluid.(C) In parallel-flow (co-current) heat exchangers, the same is also true — the cold fluid's outlet temperature can exceed the hot fluid's outlet temperature.(D) The thermal conductivity of a food material generally increases with increasing moisture content.Answer: A, B, DExplanation:(A) Correct — LMTD is precisely the tool used to represent the effective average driving temperature difference where the temperature difference between the two streams varies continuously along the exchanger length. (B) Correct — in counter-current flow, the cold fluid's outlet end is adjacent to the hot fluid's inlet end, so with sufficient exchanger length the cold outlet temperature can indeed exceed the hot fluid's outlet temperature (though not its inlet). (D) Correct — water has much higher thermal conductivity than most dry solid food constituents, so increasing moisture content generally raises the effective thermal conductivity of a food material.(C) is incorrect — in parallel-flow (co-current) exchangers, both fluids move in the same direction and their temperatures approach each other asymptotically from the same starting end, meaning the cold outlet temperature can never exceed the hot fluid's outlet temperature (unlike the counter-current case).

questions.question: [MSQ — one or more correct] Which of the following statement(s) regarding thermal processing/canning of foods is/are CORRECT?

options.A: The "12-D concept" in canning refers to a thermal process sufficient to reduce the population of Clostridium botulinum spores by 12 logarithmic (decimal) reduction cycles.
options.B: The F₀ value represents the equivalent time (in minutes) at a reference temperature of 121.1°C required to achieve a specified degree of microbial lethality.
options.C: A higher z-value indicates that a microorganism's thermal death time is highly sensitive to small changes in temperature.
options.D: Commercial sterility does not imply the complete absence of all microorganisms and spores in the container.

Q.64 Solution:• Correct Answer: A, B, D• Section: Agricultural Engineering | Sub-topic: Preservation of Food | Type: MSQ | Marks: 2Q.64  |  S7 — Dairy & Food Engineering  |  Preservation of FoodType: MSQ   |   Marks: 2Question:Which of the following statement(s) regarding thermal processing/canning of foods is/are CORRECT?(A) The "12-D concept" in canning refers to a thermal process sufficient to reduce the population of Clostridium botulinum spores by 12 logarithmic (decimal) reduction cycles.(B) The F₀ value represents the equivalent time (in minutes) at a reference temperature of 121.1°C required to achieve a specified degree of microbial lethality.(C) A higher z-value indicates that a microorganism's thermal death time is highly sensitive to small changes in temperature.(D) Commercial sterility does not imply the complete absence of all microorganisms and spores in the container.Answer: A, B, DExplanation:(A) Correct — the 12-D concept is the standard safety criterion in low-acid canning, requiring a process lethal enough to achieve a 12-log (i.e. 10¹²-fold) reduction in C. botulinum spore population. (B) Correct — F₀ is defined precisely as the equivalent process time at the standard reference temperature of 121.1°C (250°F) needed to achieve the specified lethality. (D) Correct — commercial sterility means the absence of viable microorganisms capable of growing under normal (non-refrigerated) storage and distribution conditions, not an absolute absence of all spores.(C) is incorrect — it is actually a LOWER z-value that indicates high temperature sensitivity (a small temperature change produces a large change in death time); a higher z-value means the microorganism's thermal destruction rate is comparatively less sensitive to temperature change.

questions.question: [NAT — enter numerical answer] The figure below shows the cooling curve of a food product placed in a cooling medium maintained at a constant temperature of 4°C, following Newtonian (lumped-parameter) cooling behaviour, with the product's initial temperature at 60°C.Figure: Cooling curve of a food product Using the relation (T − T∞) = (T₀ − T∞)·e^(−kt), and reading from the graph that the temperature at t = 20 min is approximately 12.9°C, estimate the cooling-rate constant k (in per minute). (Round off to three decimal places.)
questions.solution: Q.65 Solution:• Correct Answer: 0.085 to 0.098• Section: Agricultural Engineering | Sub-topic: Heat and Mass Transfer | Type: NAT | Marks: 2Q.65  |  S7 — Dairy & Food Engineering  |  Heat and Mass TransferType: NAT   |   Marks: 2Question:The figure below shows the cooling curve of a food product placed in a cooling medium maintained at a constant temperature of 4°C, following Newtonian (lumped-parameter) cooling behaviour, with the product's initial temperature at 60°C.Figure: Cooling curve of a food productUsing the relation (T − T∞) = (T₀ − T∞)·e^(−kt), and reading from the graph that the temperature at t = 20 min is approximately 12.9°C, estimate the cooling-rate constant k (in per minute). (Round off to three decimal places.)Answer: 0.085 to 0.098Explanation:(T − T∞)/(T₀ − T∞) = (12.9 − 4)/(60 − 4) = 8.9/56 = 0.1589. Taking natural log: ln(0.1589) = −1.8395. Since this equals −kt with t=20 min: k = 1.8395/20 = 0.09198 ≈ 0.092 per minute.
